draft.title: Food and fibre from biomes
card: A biome is a large region with a similar climate, plants and animals. People use biomes to get food (to eat) and fibre (such as wool, cotton and rubber, used to make goods).
Grasslands
Grasslands have flat or gently rolling land and moderate rainfall. People grow wheat there and graze sheep and cattle for meat, milk and wool.
Rainforests
Tropical rainforests are warm and wet all year. They give fruit, coffee, rubber and palm oil.
Oceans
Oceans are a source of food for people, mainly fish, which are caught from the sea.
draft.remember: Each biome gives a different mix of food and fibre, shaped by its climate and plants.

a.q: Which product is a major output from tropical rainforest biomes?
a.why: Rainforests are warm and wet all year, which suits tree crops such as palm oil. Wheat and wool come from grasslands, and fish come from oceans.
a.clue: Think of a crop that grows on trees in a warm, wet place.

b.q: Tom farms in a grassland area of Western Australia. Which pair of activities fits his biome?
opts: Catching fish and growing palm oil
Growing wheat and picking rainforest fruit
b.why: Grasslands suit wheat crops and grazing animals such as sheep. The last option is tempting because wheat is right, but rainforest fruit comes from a rainforest, not a grassland.
b.clue: Both activities must belong to grasslands, not just one.

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'The last option is tempting', but options are shown in random order. The wheat-and-rainforest-fruit option may not be last, so students could be confused. Name the option instead of its position.
Rubber is listed as a fibre. Rubber comes from latex and is not a fibre. Wool and cotton are fibres; rubber is better called a raw material or non-food product.
The clue 'a crop that grows on trees' gives the answer away. Palm oil is the only option that grows on trees, so a student can pick it without knowing what rainforests produce.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer. The why for (b) refers to 'the last option' although options are shuffled, the card calls rubber a fibre, and the clue for (a) gives the answer away.
